heading:
Experience, Key Learnings
and What It Taught Me
subtitle: A summary of my education and experience, with the lessons from each.

experience.points:
-Learned that nobody reads a 40-tab model. A one-page dashboard gets more attention than a month of spreadsheet work.
-Learned to automate anything I have to do twice. Copy-pasting monthly auto sales data builds character, but automation builds free time.
-Learned annual reports hide the best stories in the footnotes. The headline numbers are the trailer, the notes are the actual movie.
-Learned that analysis starts where the numbers stop. Anyone can calculate a growth rate, the job is explaining why it happened and whether it will last.

-Learned derivatives from the founder, then explained them to a room of strangers. Nothing tests your understanding like a question you can't Google mid-presentation.
-Sold courses in the age of free YouTube. Learned people don't pay for information, they pay for someone who makes it make sense.
-Turned market basics into a marketing campaign. Realised finance and storytelling are the same job in different outfits.

skills: Financial Modelling, 3-Statement Models, Valuation (DCF, Comps), WACC, Scenario & Sensitivity, Equity Research, Credit Analysis, Cash Runway, XIRR, Ratio Analysis, Research Writing, Industry Analysis
